Overwatch — How to use the app

This is the everyday guide to Overwatch, the operations app for Silver State Waste Solutions. It covers signing in, the driver app on a phone, the dispatch screens on a computer, and the administrator settings.

Every screenshot here was taken from practice records. Anything labeled TRAINING is safe to experiment with; anything without that label is real.

If you only do one job, read that section. Nobody needs to read all of it.

Signing in

Overwatch lives at https://sswscoapp.vercel.app. It works in any modern browser on a phone, tablet, or computer.

There is no sign-up. An administrator creates your account and hands you a temporary password in person. Sign in with your work email and that password.

On a phone it is the same screen, sized for one hand.

Set your own password straight away

Your temporary password is meant to be replaced. Open Change Password — it's at the bottom of the sidebar on a computer, and under Profile on a phone — and choose your own.

If you forget your password

Ask an administrator for a new temporary one.

Overwatch does not send email. There is no "forgot password" link, no reset message, and no invitation email. If you are waiting for an email from Overwatch, you are waiting for something that isn't coming — ask a person instead.

Where you land

You are sent to the right place automatically. Drivers land on My Jobs, dispatchers on Operations Overview, administrators on Management Overview.

If your account can open more than one workspace, the menu starts with a Portals list and you can move between them whenever you like. Administrators have all three. Most people have one, and then the list doesn't appear at all.

One thing to know if you're an office account looking at the Driver portal: My Jobs will be empty. Work is only ever dispatched to driver accounts. The portal is there so you can see exactly what a driver sees when you're training someone.

For drivers

This section is written for a phone, because that is where you'll use it.

Put it on your Home Screen

Open the site in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. It then opens like any other app, full screen, without the browser bars. The same instructions are on your Profile screen.

My Jobs

My Jobs shows only your work. Other drivers' jobs, photos, and notes are not visible to you, and yours are not visible to them.

Today and Upcoming are the two tabs. Each card shows the time, the customer, the address, the truck and dumpster, and the current status.

  • Navigate opens the address in your phone's maps app.
  • Open Job opens the full job.

Working a job

Open the job and you'll see the customer, the address, Navigate and Call Customer buttons, and a Job steps bar tracking where you are: Start, Arrive, Photo, Complete.

1. Start Route when you set off. Dispatch sees the change immediately.

2. Arrived when you get there. The action bar then offers everything you need on site.

3. Take a photo. At least one photo is required before you can complete a job — the Complete button stays greyed out and reads Add a photo to complete until you add one. Use Take Photo for the camera, or the + tile in the Photos panel to pick one you already took. JPEG, PNG, WebP, and HEIC up to 10 MB each.

4. Complete Job. You'll be asked to confirm, because it can't be undone from your phone.

Adding a note

Add Note records anything the office should know — where you left the container, a gate code, a problem on site. Type it and tap Save Note.

When you can't do the job

If something on site stops you, use Dry Run instead of completing. Say what prevented service, and dispatch is told straight away.

Time

The menu calls it Time; the screen itself is headed Time Clock.

Clock In when you start. While you're on the clock you'll see a running timer and your entries for the day.

  • Start Break and End Break — you can take as many breaks as you need, as long as each one ends.
  • Clock Out at the end of the day. You'll be asked to confirm, and told how long you worked.

Your hours are exact. There is no rounding, no overtime calculation, and nothing is deducted automatically. Dispatch reviews them.

If you clocked in late, forgot to clock out, or need time off, use Change Time or Request PTO. Your request goes to dispatch to approve or deny, and you'll see its status on this screen.

Pre-trip inspection

Pre-Trip is the daily truck inspection. Pick your truck, enter the current mileage, mark every item Pass or Fail, type your name as a signature, and submit.

Nothing is optional — the form won't submit until every item has an answer.

If you mark anything as failed, dispatch is alerted automatically. Recording a failure does not stop you being assigned that truck; it makes sure the office knows.

SOPs

SOPs holds the company's standard operating procedures. When a new one is published, it shows a Review badge — read it and tap I Have Read This SOP. The badge turns to Reviewed, and the office can see who has acknowledged the current version.

Messages

Messages is internal — announcements to everyone and direct messages with the office.

Profile

Profile has your details, your assigned truck, the Home Screen install instructions, Night Mode for driving after dark, Change Password, and Log Out.

If you lose signal

A yellow bar appears across the top: You're offline — reconnect before submitting changes.

What's already on screen stays readable, but nothing you do will save until you have signal again. Don't complete a job or clock out while that bar is showing — reconnect first, then do it.

For dispatchers

This section is written for a computer, though every screen works on a phone too.

Which menu items you see depends on what an administrator has switched on for you, so two dispatchers may not have identical menus.

Operations Overview

The daily starting point. Needs Attention across the top counts the things waiting on somebody — unassigned jobs, active jobs, time requests, failed pre-trips, open invoices — and each one is a link straight to the list.

Below that: today's job counts by status, today's jobs, an at-a-glance count of drivers, trucks and dumpsters, and recent activity.

Jobs

Every job, searchable by job number, customer, or address, filterable by status, and sortable by time, customer, or status.

New Job opens the form. Customer and address, service type and dumpster size, the scheduled date, and the driver, truck, and dumpster.

You can leave a job unassigned and come back to it — it will show in the unassigned queue on the overview. Only accounts with driver access appear in the Assign Driver list.

Following a job

Open any job to see its information, its assignments, and its status timeline. Status updates arrive as the driver works — you don't need to refresh. The job below is mid-route: the driver has already marked it arrived.

The Acknowledgement line tells you whether the assigned driver has seen the assignment yet. Photos, activity, and notes fill in as the job proceeds.

Two things you can do that a driver can't:

  • Mark Complete on a job without a photo. Overwatch will ask you to give a reason, and records it.
  • Cancel the job. A reason is required, and the truck and dumpster are released back to the pool.

Customers

The customer list, with contact details and their job history.

Add Customer takes a name, address, phone, email, and an optional group.

Trucks and dumpsters

Trucks holds each truck's number, type, status, plate, assigned driver, and notes.

Dumpsters holds the container ID, size, type, status, AirTag ID, and current location.

Locations

Locations is every truck and dumpster with its last known position, and Open in Maps for anything with an address.

This is the last reported position — operational or entered by hand, plus AirTag identifiers kept as records. It is not live GPS and it is not Apple's Find My.

Time Clock

Today's entries for every driver — clock in, breaks, clock out, hours, and whether they're currently on the clock. Exact times, no payroll rounding.

Below the table are the Time Change / PTO Requests drivers have submitted. Approve or Deny each one; the driver sees the outcome on their phone.

Absence

PTO balances and hours for the week per driver, scheduling accommodations, and the same time and PTO requests in calendar form.

Invoices

Invoice records — number, customer, amount, status, and due date — plus total receivables and a count of open invoices. New Invoice creates one, and Export CSV downloads the list.

Overwatch records invoices. It does not send them and it does not take payments.

Reports

Pick a date range, then download any of four CSV exports: Operations, Employee Time, Asset Utilization, and Invoice Records. The counts above the buttons update with the range so you can check it before downloading.

Messages

Announcements to the whole team and direct messages with drivers. Seen by… under a message you sent shows who has read it.

For administrators

Administrators can do everything above, plus the two screens below.

Management Overview

Live metrics — jobs today, active jobs, receivables, available assets — and an Exceptions list: unassigned jobs, pending time requests, failed pre-trips, inactive employees. Every number is a link to the underlying records.

Employees

The staff list, with each person's role, access, and status.

Add Employee takes an employee ID, name, email, phone, operational role, and access role. Under How they get in, choose Give them a temporary password — that's the one that works today. It sends no email; it shows a password once, on screen, for you to hand over.

The other option, Email them an invitation, needs company email sending to be configured, which it isn't. Its link is never delivered.

Write the temporary password down before you close the screen. It is shown once and can't be retrieved. If it's lost, issue a new one from the employee's page.

Access control

Open an employee to set their Role Preset — Admin, Dispatcher, or Driver — and to switch individual modules on or off. Effective Access Preview on the right lists exactly what that person will and won't see. Changes take effect immediately.

This page is also where you Issue Temporary Password if someone is locked out, and where you deactivate someone who has left.

Two accounts — Austin Marshall and the support administrator — are permanently protected. They can't be deactivated, downgraded, or have permissions removed from the app. This is deliberate: it stops a mistake or a single bad session locking every administrator out. The screen will appear to accept such a change and it will be quietly undone.

Settings

Settings is administrator-only and has a tab for each area.

Company holds the company name, address, phone, email, time zone, and date format.

App Defaults controls how long messages are kept and what invoice numbers start with.

Driver Checklist publishes the pre-trip inspection form. Type one item per line and publish; drivers get the new version immediately. Publishing a new version retires the old one.

SOP Library publishes procedures the same way. Tick Require drivers to acknowledge this SOP, and the panel at the bottom tells you who has acknowledged it and who still owes you.

Publish only approved company content here. Whatever is on this screen is what drivers are told is company policy.

Users & Roles lists active administrators. Pricing holds the price list.

Training Data creates a practice set: one customer, one truck, one dumpster, one pending unassigned job, and one zero-dollar draft invoice. All five are labeled TRAINING. It creates no logins, messages, time records, photos, SOPs, or checklists.

To remove it, choose Remove Training Data, type DELETE TRAINING DATA, and confirm. All five go together, and the removal is recorded in audit history.

When something goes wrong

If an action fails, the message ends with a reference code that looks like (Reference sfo1::abc123-...). Copy the whole code — it points straight at the matching server log.

Send the support owner:

  1. Who you were signed in as — the role, not the password.
  2. What screen you were on and what you were trying to do.
  3. Roughly what time it happened.
  4. The Reference code, if there was one.

If you got a Something Went Wrong screen instead, there's no reference code. Just describe what you were doing right before it appeared.

Never put passwords, customer or employee personal details, phone numbers, job notes, or photos in a support message. Describe the record instead — "the job for the Rainbow Blvd customer" is enough for anyone to find it.

What Overwatch does not do

None of these are missing by accident. They were agreed to be out of scope, and nothing in the app will do them:

  • No payments. Invoices are records only.
  • No payroll. Hours are exact and raw — no overtime rules, no rounding, no deductions.
  • No email. No invitations, no password resets, no notifications by mail.
  • No live GPS. Locations are last reported, not tracked.
  • No route optimization and no automatic dispatching.
  • No customer portal. Customers have no login.
  • No automated fleet maintenance.

Two more worth knowing:

  • Alerts for unassigned jobs run once a day, not every 15 minutes. The faster schedule needs a hosting upgrade.
  • Administrator sign-in is password-only. Two-factor is intentionally off. Use a strong, unique password and don't share it.

Administrators setting the system up for the first time should read docs/client-handoff.md, which covers launch configuration, protected accounts, and the accepted risks.
